newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures rallied to set a contract high on Wednesday after U.S. bonds reacted favourably to comments about inflation by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan before drifting lower on profit-taking and in tandem with German bond futures.

Traders said the start to the session was relatively active, pushing the September contract to 131.24 and matching the high for the June contract, but it failed to hang onto the early gains and soon fell back with Bunds to test 131 support.
Although the contract survived several tests of the level some said it still had room to consolidate towards 130.84.

"It was nervous this morning because of Greenspan and the French market was heavier than U.S. Treasuries," an analyst at a French brokerage said. "We left a gap at the open and then there were some stops in the Bund which was affected a bit by the mark weakness against the dollar."
He said there was little concern about Greenspan's Wednesday testimony as he was expected to say roughly the same as Tuesday.

September PIBOR was dragged higher at the open by the rally in the bond future but traders said it also came under pressure from profit-taking by non-resident investors and settled unchanged at 96.56.
The main excitement on Wednesday was on the foreign exchange markets as the dollar extended its recent gains against most European currencies.
It climbed as high as 6.1720 against the franc, its highest level since August 1991 and up 19 percent against the French unit since the beginning of the year. It was trading at 6.1557 at 1527 GMT.
